notes:
T214 session context dump — observations, ruled-out hypotheses, hazards, uncertainties, and tooling friction.

=== (1) HYPOTHESES FORMED AND RULED OUT ===

A. build.zig custom install dir for absorb (T206). Tried b.addInstallBinFile with dest_dir override -> Zig 0.16 InstallDir is an enum {.prefix, .bin, .lib, .header} with no custom variant. Compiler error. Ruled out. Fell back to addSystemCommand with cp and a named step (deploy-absorb).

B. Threaded stderr reader for runner (T214). Considered a Python threading.Thread pushing lines into a queue.Queue for the main loop. Ruled out because (a) fcntl + select is simpler, (b) thread-safety with signal handlers (SIGKILL) is messy in CPython, (c) the select timeout aligns naturally with the poll interval. The non-blocking approach works correctly in all three kill modes tested.

C. managent ping subprocess per progress line (T214). Considered calling subprocess.run(['managent', 'ping', '--note', ...]) on every [progress] line to feed the kanban. Ruled out because (a) _emit_heartbeat writes directly to heartbeat.jsonl — same file, same format, (b) a subprocess per progress line adds ~10-50ms latency and a fork per event, (c) the heartbeat write is idempotent — multiple heartbeats per task are expected by managent liveness.

=== (2) HAZARDS, SMELLS, FRAGILE ASSUMPTIONS ===

A. fcntl is Unix-only. The runner already depends on /proc walk, ps, os.setsid(), and SIGKILL — all Unix-specific. This is fine for the project's macOS/Linux hosts. A Windows port would need a different stderr-reading strategy (overlapped I/O or threads). Not investigated because out of scope.

B. Progress detection is substring-based: any stderr line containing '[progress]' counts. A line like 'error: [progress] bar not found' would be a false positive timer reset. Deliberate tradeoff for simplicity; the cost of a false positive is a timer reset (not data loss). Could tighten with a regex anchor (^\[progress\]) in a future pass.

C. _drain_stderr switches stderr back to blocking mode to read tail data. If the child crashed leaving stderr in a broken-pipe state, this could hang. proc.wait() already completed so stderr should be fully buffered; the risk is theoretical. Mitigation: the drain runs after proc.poll() returns not-None, so the child is dead and stderr is at EOF.

D. Heartbeat on progress uses sentinel values (-1 for CPU, -1 for RSS) when no RSS/CPU measurement was taken at that moment. managent liveness may display 'wall: -1.0s cpu: -1.0s rss: -1 MB' for these intermediate heartbeats. Confusing but harmless. Could use null/absent fields instead, but the heartbeat schema expects numbers. SPECULATION: a future liveness display should distinguish 'no measurement' from 'zero'.

E. The deploy-absorb build step (addSystemCommand with cp) has a potential race: if zig-out/bin/weizigo-absorb doesn't exist yet (first build or clean), the cp fails silently because addSystemCommand only tracks step ordering, not file existence. On a clean checkout, 'zig build deploy-absorb' might fail. SPECULATION: should check return code of cp or use b.addInstallBinFile with a custom prefix path.

=== (3) UNCERTAINTIES IN OWN DELIVERABLE ===

A. --progress-timeout default 600s (10 min). The brief says 'propose a default; 600 s is a starting point, argue for better.' I used 600 because the brief suggested it, but I have NO DATA on actual fixpoint sweep durations on 4x4. If a single sweep takes >10 min (plausible for late-stage fixpoint on the full 4x4 state space), the watchdog would kill a correctly-progressing build. I would not defend 600 s without a measured sweep-duration distribution.

B. Heartbeat integration with managent liveness not tested end-to-end. I verified heartbeats are written to untracked/heartbeat.jsonl in the correct JSONL format, and the format matches readHeartbeats in src/managent/main.zig. But I did not run 'managent liveness' to confirm it parses progress-emitted heartbeats correctly for a real in_progress task. It should work — the schema is the same — but untested.

C. The total_chunks calculation in oracle_v2_build.zig uses integer ceiling division: (file_bytes.len + CHUNK - 1) / CHUNK. This is correct for usize. The line is now reverted (held for T212) but when re-applied, verify under ReleaseFast (assertions are no-ops).

D. The runner's --poll-ms default of 250ms means a progress line could take up to 250ms to be detected. At the default --progress-timeout of 600s, this is negligible (0.04% jitter). But at very short timeouts (e.g. --progress-timeout 1), the poll interval dominates the effective timeout. Not documented; probably fine since short timeouts are not the intended use case.

=== (4) TOOLING/BRIEF/DOC FRICTION ===

A. managent done deliverable parser vs brief frontmatter (T206). The done command's parseDeliverablesFromBundle scans for 'Deliverables:' substring in the bundle body. The T206 brief had '**Deliverables:**' in its markdown frontmatter (bold formatting). The parser matched this, extracted nonsense tokens ('**', '1', 'print', 'so', 'and', '`untracked/absorption.md`'), and rejected the done command with 5 'missing' deliverables. I had to edit the brief to rename '**Deliverables:**' -> '**Deliverables (task brief):**' and add a real 'Deliverables:' line. This is a fragile parser-trigger pattern; any brief with a Deliverables section will hit this. The parser should either anchor on a specific format or only scan below a marker line. SPECULATION: this will bite every agent whose bundle contains 'Deliverables:' in prose.

B. suggest stdout format changed mid-T204-session. When I wrote the regression test, suggest printed 'You are <model>/<id>. <slug>'. By the time I ran it after the fix, the format had changed to 'Follow untracked/<id>-<slug>.md'. The test check 3 grep for model name broke. This suggests suggest output is unstable across versions — tests that parse suggest output are fragile.

C. build.ig addSystemCommand doesn't track file dependencies, only step ordering. The deploy-absorb step depends on the install step (which writes zig-out/bin/weizigo-absorb), but there's no file-level dependency — if the install step runs but the file isn't written (build error in another artifact?), the cp would silently fail. SPECULATION: this is a general fragility of build.zig's addSystemCommand for deploy steps.

D. gen-indices imported subprocess and json but only used subprocess for the kanban snapshot (dropped in T206). json was also unused after the kanban drop. I removed subprocess from the import but left json — a minor lint. No functional impact.
